{{Quote|Lord Sidious, we have retrieved the droid control program and struck a mortal blow to the Naboo.|Nute Gunray to Darth Sidious after the battle|audio=GunrayIsHappy.flac|<ref name="GB" />}}
During the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]] in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], the [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Harte Secur]] was '''captured''' by the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]]. Shortly after the Trade Federation's landing on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]], a [[droid control program]] was stolen by a [[Naboo (people)/Legends|Naboo]] [[Force Command Two|strike team]], rendering a portion of the [[Trade Federation Droid Army/Legends|Trade Federation Droid Army]] deactivated. Fearing that the Naboo could use the program to turn the Droid Army against him, [[Viceroy of the Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation Viceroy]] [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]] dispatched the [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|B1-series battle droid]] [[OOM-9/Legends|OOM-9]] to retrieve it with the help of a task force of [[Droideka/Legends|droidekas]], a [[bio cannon]], and a [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidian]] [[Unidentified Neimoidian technician (Harte Secur)|technician]].

The task force made their way to the research center south of Harte Secur where the program was kept, [[Death/Legends|killing]] any Naboo [[Trooper/Legends|troopers]] in their path and using the bio [[Cannon/Legends|cannon]] to destroy [[Turret/Legends|turrets]]. After breaking into the research outpost and retrieving the program, OOM-9 brought it to the [[Deactivated Camp|camp]] where the deactivated [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]] stood, and the technician was able to reactivate the droids. Gunray then ordered OOM-9 to attack Harte Secur with his restored [[Army/Legends|army]]. At the city, the droidekas gunned down the troopers protecting its entrance and the bio cannon was used to destroy several turrets and the city's [[command center]], solidifying the Trade Federation's victory. The company occupied the ruins of Harte Secur in the aftermath of the battle until they were [[Liberation of Harte Secur|driven]] out by the [[Gungan Grand Army/Legends|Gungan Grand Army]].

==Prelude==
{{Quote|OOM-14 has allowed the Naboo to make off with a precious droid control program.|Nute Gunray to OOM-9|audio=OOM-14Sucks.flac|<ref name="GB" />}}
[[File:Force_Command_Two.png|thumb|right|300px|Naboo forces stole one of the droid control programs, putting the Trade Federation's invasion at risk.]]
In [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] and its [[Trade Federation Droid Army/Legends|Droid Army]] commenced the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|invasion]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] in protest of [[Senate Resolution BR-0371]]. Their initial attack successfully [[Subjugation of Parrlay|destroyed]] the equipment Naboo used for offworld communications, but their plans came to a halt when one of their five [[droid control program]]s that kept the Droid Army active was stolen from the [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|B1-series battle droid]] [[OOM-14/Legends|OOM-14]] by the [[Royal Naboo Security Forces/Legends|Royal Naboo Security Forces]] team [[Force Command Two]]. The program was taken to a [[Research Center]] south of the [[Naboo (people)/Legends|Naboo]] [[City/Legends|city]] [[Harte Secur]] to be analyzed, and without it OOM-14's [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]]&mdash;a division of forty-eight B1-Series battle [[Droid/Legends|droids]] and eight [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|missile battle droids]]&mdash;was left motionless at the [[Deactivated Camp]] south of the research center. The Trade Federation leadership, including [[Viceroy of the Trade Federation/Legends|Viceroy]] [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]], feared that the Naboo could [[Slicer/Legends|hack]] and duplicate the program to turn the Droid Army against them.<ref name="GB" />

The Trade Federation thus jammed communications around Harte Secur to prevent the program from being spread, which kept the situation tenuously under control. Gunray deployed his most trusted droid, the B1 battle droid [[OOM-9/Legends|OOM-9]], to retrieve the program and then destroy Harte Secur.<ref name="Prima">[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Prima's Official Strategy Guide|''Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds'': Prima's Official Strategy Guide]]</ref> OOM-9 arrived at the Deactivated Camp in his personal [[Armored Assault Tank/Legends|Heavy Armored Assault Tank]], and was later joined by a strike force delivered by a [[Neimoidian transport]] that included five heavy [[Droideka/Legends|droidekas]], one [[bio cannon]], and a [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidian]] [[Unidentified Neimoidian technician (Harte Secur)|technician]], who was provided to handle and reactivate the droid control program. Gunray ordered OOM-9 to protect the technician at all costs,<ref name="GB" /> with the technician being loaded into OOM-9's AAT for protection.<ref name="Prima" />

==The battle==
===Retrieving the program===
{{Quote|Droid control program recovered.|OOM-9|audio=DroidControlProgramRecovered.flac|<ref name="GB" />}}
[[File:Droids_have_the_research.png|thumb|left|350px|The droids attack the research center.]]
The task force followed a paved path east of the camp to find the research center. They encountered a group of fifteen Naboo [[Security Guard/Legends|security guards]] standing in close formation, and the droids used the bio [[Cannon/Legends|cannon]] to fire a shot at them from a safe distance while the droidekas eliminated the survivors.<ref name="Prima" /> The group then proceeded north to a shallow crossing point of a [[Water/Legends|river]], which was guarded by<ref name="GB" /> two [[Tuskcat Trooper]]s,<ref name="CC" /> four [[Champion (vehicle)|champion]] [[Repulsorcraft/Legends|repulsorcrafts]], and two light [[Turret/Legends|turrets]].<ref name="GB" /> OOM-9 used the droidekas to draw the defenders closer to them to avoid risking damage from the turrets, keeping the droidekas out of range of<ref name="Prima" /> the Tuskcat Troopers' [[Flamethrower/Legends|flamethrowers]].<ref name="CC" /> After the mounted troopers and [[Speeder/Legends|speeders]] were destroyed, the bio cannon destroyed the turrets, as it was able to target them from beyond their firing range. The droids moved forward with the goal of destroying any turrets or troopers they encountered,<ref name="Prima" /> which included another pair of turrets on the other side of the river.<ref name="GB" />

The droids encountered and [[Death/Legends|killed]] a pair of troopers on the other side of the river, and on the path to the east they encountered one [[Steadfast (tank)|Steadfast]], a powerful Naboo [[Tank/Legends|tank]], along with another turret nearby,<ref name="GB" /> which they destroyed with the cannon.<ref name="Prima" /> At the entrance to the research center the droids encountered eight [[Elite Royal Crusader]]s stationed outside it, along with two turrets and five troopers stationed inside the walls.<ref name="GB" /> OOM-9 had the cannon fire at the closest turret while the droidekas stood in front of it for protection, having no difficulty gunning down the defenders that ran out to protect the research center. With the area cleared of opposition, the cannon moved closer to destroy the remaining turret and the research center's [[Power core/Legends|power core]]. Afterward, OOM-9 drove into the ruins and collected the droid control program into his AAT,<ref name="Prima" /> reporting his success to Gunray, who instructed him to return to the camp. The droids returned through the path they had taken to the Deactivated Camp, where the [[Technician/Legends|technician]] was able to reactivate the droids there.<ref name="GB" />

===Punishing Harte Secur===
{{Quote|Your army is online. Destroy Harte Secur!|Nute Gunray to OOM-9|audio=ArmyOnline.flac|<ref name="GB" />}}
With the Droid Army fully operational, Gunray ordered OOM-9 to destroy Harte Secur.<ref name="GB" /> While organizing his new troops for the assault, the army was attacked by<ref name="Prima" /> [[N-1L Light Starfighter]]s from the [[Naboo Airforce]], who had an [[Harte Secur Airbase|airbase]] nearby.<ref name="GB" /> OOM-9's newly acquired missile battle droids were able to shoot the fighters down. With his troops prepared, the Droid Army marched for Harte Secur, with OOM-9, five B1 battle droids, two missile battle droids, and the Neimoidian technician remaining at the camp, with the latter garrisoned inside its [[command center]].<ref name="Prima" />

{{GameMechanics|legends=1|Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds}}
Acting on a recommendation made in a reconnaissance report, OOM-9 attacked and destroyed the [[Airbase/Legends|airbase]].<ref name="GB" />
{{Endgame}}

[[File:Harte_Secur_ruins.png|thumb|right|300px|Ruins in the aftermath of the battle]]
The droids continued up the path that the task force had taken earlier, but at a crossroads they continued north instead of heading south as they had done previously. At an entrance to the city guarded by two medium turrets and several troopers, the droidekas carefully avoided the turrets to gun down the troopers, keeping the rest of the battle droids at a distance to avoid them getting in the way. The bio cannon then destroyed the turrets. Behind them, a small courtyard with a large archway led into the main courtyard of Harte Secur, at the north of it lay the Naboo command center, the Trade Federation's target.<ref name="Prima" />

The cannon rolled into the courtyard and opened fire on the command center while the droids clogged the entrance and destroyed the further streams of [[Soldier/Legends|soldier]] and mechs sent by the Naboo,<ref name="Prima" /> including sixteen troopers, seven Royal Crusaders, four Steadfasts, four Champions, two Heavy Champions, three [[Naboo energy catapult]]s, four [[V-19 landspeeder]]s,<ref name="GB" /> and two Advanced Tuskcat Troopers.<ref name="CC" /> Harte Secur was not able to counter the Trade Federation's superior numbers,<ref name="Prima" /> and once the command center was destroyed they took control of the ruined city, taking some of its inhabitants [[Prisoner/Legends|prisoner]].<ref name="GB" />

==Aftermath==
{{Quote|You have performed beyond your parameters.|Nute Gunray congratulating OOM-9 after the battle|audio=OOM9reallygood.flac|<ref name="GB" />}}
[[File:Camp_Six.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Camp Six, a Trade Federation base built near the city after the battle]]
Gunray was impressed with OOM-9's leadership in the battle and placed him in [[Commanding officer/Legends|command]] of the [[Invasion of Spinnaker|invasion]] of another major Naboo city, [[Spinnaker/Legends|Spinnaker]]. The [[Viceroy/Legends|viceroy]] also reported the successful attack to [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]], his secret benefactor. The Trade Federation heavily fortified the ruins of Harte Secur, keeping the city's outer shell intact while establishing their own settlements on the interior. They also established [[Camp Six]] nearby, where they captured the planet's [[Homeworld/Legends|native]] [[Fambaa/Legends|fambaas]] to skin and sell. Following the [[Capture of Theed/Legends|fall]] of the Human [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of [[Theed/Legends|Theed]]<ref name="GB" /> on the day after the Trade Federation's landing,<ref name="Inside">''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars: Episode I]]''</ref> the company began to focus on fighting the [[Gungan/Legends|Gungans]], an [[Amphibian/Legends|amphibious]] [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] on Naboo. A captured [[Unidentified mariner|mariner]] from Harte Secur<ref name="GB" /> told OOM-9<ref name="Endgame">{{StoryCite|story=End Game|book=Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|bformatted=''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' novelization, 2012 edition}}</ref> about [[Ganne]], the Gungan [[Boss/Legends|Boss]] of the city [[Rellias]], which led to an extended search for the city and eventually an [[Siege of Otoh Gunga|attack]] on the Gungan capital [[Otoh Gunga/Legends|Otoh Gunga]].<ref name="GB" />

In the aftermath of the attack on Otoh Gunga, Boss [[Rugor Nass/Legends|Rugor Nass]] of the Gungans formed an alliance with [[Monarch of Naboo/Legends|Queen]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] of the Naboo. To retake their planet, they planned to march the [[Gungan Grand Army/Legends|Gungan Grand Army]] toward occupied Theed to draw the Droid Army out. The Grand Army relied on mounting fambaas with [[Deflector shield generator/Legends|shield generators]] for their strategy, so they established a base near Harte Secur and [[Liberation of Harte Secur|attacked]] Camp Six to free fambaas and outfit them with shields.<ref name="GB" /> The Gungans then attacked Harte Secur and destroyed the Trade Federation's command center there to demonstrate the Grand Army's capabilities<ref name="Prima" /> and hasten the Droid Army's emergence from Theed. Both armies later [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|clashed]] on the [[Great Grass Plains/Legends|Great Grass Plains]], ending in a Gungan victory.<ref name="GB" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Gameplay options===
[[File:HarteSecurAirbase-SWGB.png|thumb|right|260px|The player controls the Trade Federation and has the option to attack Harte Secur Airbase in the battle.]]
The capture of Harte Secur was first mentioned in [[Prima Games]]' [[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Prima's Official Strategy Guide|strategy guide]] by [[Steven L. Kent]]<ref name="Prima" />&mdash;released on [[November 7]], [[2001]]<ref name="PrimaDate">{{Amazon|url=Star-Wars-Galactic-Battlegrounds-Official/dp/0761537503|text=Star Wars Galactic Battlegrounds: Prima's Official Strategy Guide}}</ref>&mdash;for the [[LucasArts]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]'',<ref name="GB" /> released on [[November 11]], 2001.<ref name="GBDate">{{GameSpot|url=games/star-wars-galactic-battlegrounds|text=Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds}}</ref> The attack constitutes the second level, titled "Behind the Lines," of the Trade Federation campaign, where the player is tasked with retrieving the droid control program and destroying Harte Secur. Upon recovering the program, the player has the option of creating additional units and buildings for their army and is provided with resources to do so.<ref name="GB" /> However, the strategy guide describes the level as a seek-and-destroy mission that can be completed without creating additional units.<ref name="Prima" />

The player is faced with two enemy factions: Harte Secur and Harte Secur Airbase. The game recommends that the player destroy Harte Secur Airbase to protect their forces, but it is not essential for victory. While it remains operational, Harte Secur Airbase may send N-1L Light Starfighters and [[NB-1 Royal Bomber]]s to attack the player. The level can be lost if either OOM-9 or the Neimoidian technician are killed. The game originally featured the Naboo mounted troopers riding [[Kaadu/Legends|kaadu]],<ref name="GB" /> but those mounts were changed to [[tusk cat]]s in the [[2002]] expansion [[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Clone Campaigns|''Clone Campaigns'']].<ref name="CC" /> The strategy guide suggests prioritizing the safety of the bio cannon to secure an easier victory and recommends that the player follow the eastern path from their base to reach the research center and that they should clear the path of any units on their way to keep the path safe for the return journey.<ref name="Prima" /> However, two aquatic [[Transport (Royal Naboo)|Naboo transports]] are located near the research center and can be acquired if the player's units come close enough to them, shortening the time taken to transport units between the research center and the player's camp.<ref name="GB" />

===Differences between difficulty levels and the strategy guide===
Different numbers of units appear for the player to fight depending on the difficulty level selected by the player,<ref name="GB" /> and differing numbers of units are given by the strategy guide as well.<ref name="Prima" /> After defeating the group of fifteen troopers on the path to the research center, the player may encounter two mounted troopers and two light turrets in the easy difficulty, an additional four strike mechs in the moderate difficulty, and another pair of light turrets on the other side of the river in hard difficulty.<ref name="GB" /> The strategy guide states that two mounted troopers, one V-19 [[Landspeeder/Legends|landspeeder]], and the turrets await the player there. The guide also notes that the player can destroy a Naboo gazebo in that area with a single shot from their cannon, but it has no strategic impact<ref name="Prima" /> The Champion on the path to the research center only appears in the hard difficulty,<ref name="GB" /> and the strategy guide states that several troopers, mounted troopers, and turrets await the player there.<ref name="Prima" />

[[File:Harte_Secur_minimap.png|thumb|left|250px|Full view of the in-game minimap at the start of the battle. Naboo units are in yellow and orange, Trade Federation forces are in green, and the Gungans are in purple.]]
The strategy guide mentions that the player will encounter a group of [[PKN-49 worker droid|worker droids]] gathering [[Carbon/Legends|carbon]] on the path to Harte Secur. It states that they can be destroyed as long as the player is cautious of the nearby turret, and their units may go astray if they follow the fleeing workers.<ref name="Prima" /> However, the worker droids do not appear in the game. In the easy difficulty, Harte Secur is defended by sixteen troopers, seven Royal Crusaders, four V-19 landspeeders, three Naboo energy catapults,<ref name="GB" /> and two advanced Tuskcat Troopers.<ref name="CC" /> In the moderate difficulty, four Champions and two Heavy Champions are added. In the hard difficulty, four Steadfasts and five [[Deflector shield/Legends|shield]] generators are added.<ref name="GB" /> The strategy guide describes the layout of Harte Secur differently to the finished game. An image shows the command center not in the courtyard but on the other side of the treeline to the north. Nevertheless, it recommends entering the courtyard despite its strategic vulnerability, as the cannon can still take the command center down from that position.<ref name="Prima" />

===Easter eggs and unused material===
{{Quote|I am sending EEK-176 to replace you at Harte Secur.|Unused dialogue by Nute Gunray|audio=EEK-176Replacement.flac|<ref name="GB" />}}
[[File:The_Three_Amigos.png|thumb|right|250px|Using cheats, three familiar faces can be found in the level.]]
Near Harte Secur, the player can find a Gungan settlement which they can choose to attack, although that encounter would be non-[[canon]]ical, as the game portrays the Trade Federation as unaware of the Gungans' existence until later in the invasion. If the player uses a cheat code to view the whole map, they can find [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], [[Jar Jar Binks/Legends|Jar Jar Binks]], and a Gungan [[Bongo Scout|frigate]] in an inaccessible area in the eastern corner of the map, suggesting<ref name="GB" /> that the meeting between the three characters on Naboo as portrayed in the [[1999]] [[prequel trilogy]] film, [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']], may have been occurring<ref name="TPM">{{Film|I}}</ref> concurrently to the attack on Harte Secur. If the player gets one of their units near the three characters, they will be able to use them in the battle. In several unused audio files, Gunray informs OOM-9 that [[EEK-176]], a droid from the previous mission in the Trade Federation campaign, "Beachhead," will take his place at Harte Secur to allow OOM-9 to command the invasion of Spinnaker.<ref name="GB" />
